subtitle: Lesson 12 · Linux Fundamentals I — The Shell & Filesystem

eyebrow: Where am I, and what's here?
code:
$ pwd
/home/alice/projects

$ ls -la
drwxr-xr-x  4 alice alice 4096 notes.txt
-rw-r--r--  1 alice alice  512 scripts

$ cd scripts
caption: pwd prints your location, ls -la lists contents (long format + hidden files), cd moves you.

code:
$ mkdir backups
$ touch backups/readme.txt
$ cp notes.txt backups/notes.txt
$ mv backups/readme.txt backups/README.txt
$ rm -r backups
caption: mkdir, touch, cp, mv, rm — there's no Recycle Bin, rm is permanent.

code:
$ cat notes.txt
Project kickoff: Oct 28

$ less /var/log/syslog
# one screen at a time, / to search, q to quit
caption: cat dumps a whole file; less pages through anything longer than a screenful.
grep searches what's inside files; find searches which files exist, and where.
